beats.visual: In the ink-wash editorial world, a single lipstick tube stands beside a nearly empty coin purse on a modest home table, with the protagonist leaning in from the opposite side as if recognizing the connection.
beats.purpose: introduce the lipstick effect as a link between limited money and a small cosmetic purchase
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium three-quarter home-table shot; hero leaning toward an upright lipstick and open coin purse; warm lamp-lit domestic setting; asymmetrical composition with lipstick-red focal accent on the right
beats.continuity: moves from the book-retrieval opening into the first concrete example, keeping the same domestic economic world but introducing lipstick as the new focal object

beats.visual: A close overhead ink-wash still life shows a lipstick tube casting a soft shadow shaped like a small recurring ripple beside scattered coins, suggesting the alternate name without any lettering.
beats.purpose: show that lipstick syndrome is another name for the same recurring consumer phenomenon
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight overhead still life; no hero; lipstick centered over a ripple-like wash shadow with three loose coins; cool overcast tabletop light; circular composition
beats.continuity: shifts away from the protagonist to an abstract object-focused interpretation of the same concept

beats.narration_slice: The theory starts with tighter budgets.
beats.visual: The protagonist sits at a small kitchen table tightening the drawstring of a coin purse while a few coins and a blank-lined shopping slip sit nearby.
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide side-angle kitchen-table scene; hero seated and pulling a coin-purse cord tight; sparse coins and abstract shopping slip; gray daylight through a window; horizontal left-heavy composition
beats.continuity: returns to the protagonist and turns the abstract idea into a physical household budgeting action

beats.visual: An unlabeled balance-like economic diagram shows several large luxury silhouettes sinking out of the illustration window while one tiny lipstick remains above the cutoff line.
beats.purpose: explain that expensive discretionary purchases are removed first
beats.visual_fingerprint: centered simplified economic diagram; no hero; oversized handbag, appliance, and leisure-object silhouettes dropping downward; tiny lipstick isolated above; flat cream background with charcoal geometry
beats.continuity: converts the tighter-budget action into a simplified visual rule about which purchases disappear

beats.visual: Through a modest home window, the protagonist looks toward a distant muted car parked behind a closed gate, while the coin purse rests untouched on the interior sill.
beats.purpose: show a major purchase being postponed
beats.visual_fingerprint: over-the-shoulder interior-to-exterior shot; hero seen from behind at window; distant parked car beyond closed gate; cool daylight; strong depth composition with purse in foreground
beats.continuity: takes one large luxury from the prior diagram and turns it into a specific postponed real-world purchase

beats.visual: A closed travel suitcase sits pushed beneath a hallway bench, gathering a faint wash of dust while the protagonist walks past carrying groceries instead.
beats.purpose: show discretionary travel being delayed when money is tight
beats.visual_fingerprint: low-angle hallway shot; hero legs passing with a modest grocery bag; dormant suitcase tucked under bench; warmer late-afternoon domestic light; diagonal movement across frame
beats.continuity: continues the sequence of postponed large expenses but changes from an exterior car view to an indoor travel symbol and active everyday spending

beats.narration_slice: But lipstick may still feel affordable.
beats.visual: At a modest cosmetics counter, a hand holds one small lipstick above a few remaining coins, with larger blurred products receding into muted gray wash behind it.
beats.purpose: show lipstick remaining within reach despite a reduced budget
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight hand-level counter shot; cropped hand but no full hero; lipstick held above a tiny coin cluster; subdued shop setting; shallow layered composition with restrained red focal point
beats.continuity: pivots from what is postponed to the small purchase that can still fit within the remaining budget

beats.visual: The protagonist stands before a small mirror at home, holding the newly purchased lipstick near the chest and showing a subtle relieved smile rather than a glamorous pose.
beats.purpose: show the emotional comfort attached to a modest affordable purchase
beats.visual_fingerprint: intimate mirror-side medium close-up; hero softly smiling with lipstick held near chest; warm evening lamp glow; curved mirror edge framing the face; no coins visible
beats.continuity: moves from affordability at the counter to the quiet emotional payoff of the purchase at home

beats.narration_slice: After the 2001 downturn, Leonard Lauder noticed stronger lipstick sales.
beats.visual: A restrained recession-era cosmetics counter is shown from above with many lipstick tubes being gathered into a sales tray while other product spaces remain sparse, using quantity alone to imply stronger sales.
beats.purpose: illustrate the historical observation that lipstick sales appeared stronger after the 2001 downturn
beats.visual_fingerprint: high overhead retail-counter scene; no hero; clustered lipstick tubes filling a shallow tray while surrounding shelves stay sparse; cool commercial daylight; dense red-accent cluster in lower center
beats.continuity: expands from one person's small purchase to a broader retail pattern without introducing readable historical labels

beats.narration_slice: He called it the lipstick index.
beats.visual: A simple ink-wash economic metaphor shows a single lipstick tube acting like the needle of an unlabeled gauge, angled upward over a semicircular charcoal scale with no marks or numbers.
beats.purpose: explain the idea of treating lipstick sales as an economic indicator
beats.visual_fingerprint: minimal centered gauge metaphor; no hero; lipstick used as upward-pointing indicator needle; ivory paper field; semicircular charcoal arc with no labels or ticks
beats.continuity: turns the observed retail pattern into the indicator concept associated with the lipstick index

beats.visual: Two uneven pools of ink spread in opposite directions around a lipstick placed between them, one wash rising and the other fading, conveying conflicting findings without charts or labels.
beats.purpose: show that later evidence did not point consistently in one direction
beats.visual_fingerprint: abstract top-down paper composition; no hero; lipstick horizontal at center dividing one expanding dark wash from one receding pale wash; neutral daylight; bilateral but deliberately uneven balance
beats.continuity: softens the apparent certainty of the previous indicator image by replacing the clean upward signal with visibly conflicting outcomes

beats.narration_slice: Some found higher cosmetics spending among certain groups during recessions.
beats.visual: A small group of differently styled shoppers at an understated cosmetics counter each reaches toward modest beauty items while muted recession-gray storefront shapes sit beyond the window.
beats.purpose: show that some research observed increased cosmetics spending among particular consumer groups during recessions
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide oblique shop-interior scene; three distinct shoppers reaching toward small cosmetics; no protagonist; gray storefront visible outside; staggered triangular composition with several restrained red accents
beats.continuity: takes one side of the mixed-results idea and depicts the specific finding of increased cosmetics spending among some groups

beats.narration_slice: Others found lipstick wasn't a reliable economic signal.
beats.visual: A lipstick stands beside a wavering, broken charcoal trend line that changes direction repeatedly, while a steady household coin stack sits separately in the foreground.
beats.purpose: show that lipstick sales do not consistently track the wider economy
beats.visual_fingerprint: angled tabletop diagram-scene hybrid; no hero; lipstick at rear beside erratic broken trend stroke; stable coin stack isolated in foreground; muted cool lighting; strong near-far separation
beats.continuity: presents the opposing research conclusion by contrasting an unstable lipstick signal with a separate grounded money reference

beats.narration_slice: It's a theory about consumer psychology.
beats.visual: The protagonist sits quietly at the home table between a closed coin purse and a lipstick, one hand near each, looking thoughtfully from necessity to comfort as soft ink-wash shadows merge beneath the objects.
beats.purpose: sum up the lipstick effect as a theory about how people emotionally choose between restraint and small comforts
beats.visual_fingerprint: balanced frontal medium-wide home scene; hero centered in reflective pose between coin purse and lipstick; warm evening lamp light; two object shadows merging beneath the hands; calm symmetrical composition
beats.continuity: returns from competing research findings to the protagonist and reframes the whole sequence as a question of consumer psychology
